Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown

the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

name: arc-pack-spatial-patterns
description: Use when an ARC grid has several separated small colored motifs to extract and pack in spatial order. Preserve motif cells and infer the output axis from their source placement.
---

# Pack separated motifs in spatial order

Use this pattern when a sparse grid contains multiple disconnected, similarly sized motifs (often 3×3), each in a different nonzero color, and the output appears to consolidate them.

1. Find each connected nonzero component and record its color and bounding box. Keep zeros inside the box: they are part of the motif's shape.
2. Compare the components' positions. If they are laid out mainly from left to right, order by horizontal position and concatenate the cropped motifs horizontally. If laid out mainly top to bottom, order by vertical position and concatenate vertically.
3. Remove only empty space between/outside components; do not rotate, recolor, resize, or reorder by color. Output dimensions are the motif height by summed widths for horizontal packing, or summed heights by motif width for vertical packing.
4. Verify each output crop exactly matches the corresponding source motif and that the ordering follows source position.

Evidence from demos: three separate 3×3 motifs were consolidated into a 3×9 output when their arrangement was horizontal; three motifs in a vertical arrangement became a 9×3 output. In the horizontal case, order followed left-to-right positions (not numeric color order). In the vertical case, order followed top-to-bottom positions.

Caution: use the full bounding box of each motif, including zero cells. Infer packing axis from the source layout rather than assuming a fixed orientation.",
